summary: Osamu Izumoji is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who held posts at Kyoto Prefectural University and Ryukoku University.

Osamu Oba was a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Kansai University (~1948–1953) and held posts at Kansai University (~1957–1997), Kogakkan University (~1997–2002), and the University of the Sacred Heart.

Osamu Takata was a Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology scholar who studied under Baiei Henmi. He served as a lecturer at Tohoku University (attested 1961) and as head of the fine arts department at Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties (attested 1967).

Linguist Osborn Bergin studied at University College Cork, the School of Irish Learning under Kuno Meyer, and the University of Freiburg under Heinrich Zimmer. He held posts at University College Dublin (~1909–1940) and the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies (~1940–1941).
Oscar Botto was an Indologist who studied under Mario Vallauri. He served as president of CESMEO and was an Emeritus Professor of Indology at the University of Turin (attested 2005).

Oscar Flex worked in linguistics and Indology. He served as a missionary for the Gossner Evangelical Lutheran Church in 1861, joined the Society for the Propagation of the Gospel in Foreign Parts in 1877, and was a superintendent at East-India Tea Company.

Oscar Lewis was an Indologist who earned his B.A. from City College of New York (~1932–1936) and Ph.D. from Columbia University (~1936–1940). He held posts at Brooklyn College, Washington University in St. Louis, the University of Washington, and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.

Oscar Luis Chavarria-Aguilar worked in linguistics and Indology, earning degrees from UC Berkeley and the University of Pennsylvania. He held posts at Deccan College, the American University in Cairo, the University of Michigan, the University of Rochester, CCNY, and the National University of Costa Rica.

Indologist and linguist Oskar Frankfurter studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Göttingen. He served as head of the National Library of Thailand (1905–1917) and later taught Thai at the University of Hamburg (1921–1922).

Linguist Oskar Johann Wiedemann studied under Leo Meyer at the University of Tartu, where he earned his degrees between 1879 and 1889. He served as a Privatdozent at the University of Tartu from 1887 to 1890.

Oskar Kressler worked in Japanology and Indology, studying at Leipzig under Ernst Windisch, Geneva, and Strasbourg under Ernst Leumann. He later served as Privatdozent (1932) and extraordinary professor of Japanology (1939–1949) at the University of Bonn.

Indologist and linguist Oskar von Hinüber studied at Tübingen, Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Mainz under Karl Hoffmann and Paul Thieme. He held posts at Mainz (1965–1981), the Nepal Research Centre, and as professor at the University of Freiburg (1981–2006).

Osmund Bopearachchi studied at the University of Kelaniya, Panthéon-Sorbonne University, and Paris-Sorbonne University. He served at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique beginning in 1989 and as an adjunct professor at the University of California, Berkeley (~2014).

Osvald Sirén was a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology who completed his doctoral work at the University of Helsinki. He held posts at Stockholm University (1908–1923), the Guimet Museum (1924–1925), and as a keeper at Nationalmuseum (1926–1945).

Oswald Richter specialized in Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. He completed his Ph.D. under Karl Brugmann at the University of Leipzig (~1892–1897) and held posts at the Museum of Ethnology, Dresden (1898) and the Ethnological Museum of Berlin (1904).

Otakar Klíma studied Iranian, Central Asian studies, and linguistics at Charles University under Bedřich Hrozný, Vincenc Lesný, and Jan Rypka. From 1953 to 1973, he served as head of the Near Eastern section at the Czechoslovak Academy of Sciences.

Otakar Pertold studied Indology and religious studies at Charles University and under scholars including Josef Zubatý, Wilhelm Geiger, and Paul Deussen. He spent his career primarily at Charles University (~1919–1955), eventually becoming an ordinary professor in 1934.

Indologist Othmar Frank studied Sanskrit under Alexander Hamilton and attended the University of Paris. He held teaching posts at Banz Abbey, Kaiser-Heinrich-Gymnasium Bamberg, and the universities of Bamberg (~1802–1803), Würzburg (1821), and Munich (1826).
Indologist Otoya Tanaka studied at the University of Tokyo (~1924–1928) under Naoshiro Tsuji. He served as a professor at Chuo University from ~1951 to 1974.

Linguist and Iranian/Central Asian scholar Otto Albert Paul studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Munich, where he worked under Wilhelm Geiger. In 1941, he served as director of the Institut zur Erforschung der Judenfrage.
